runner: Headless Chrome loading the built desktop UI with an isolated mock Tauri invoke bridge; no native app, production service, external provider, or user data was used.
assertions: Provider management opens with an existing provider.
Third-party and custom API modes retain separate drafts.
Fetch, search, select-visible, deselect-all, and Add selected update the draft only.
Duplicate model IDs are rejected before a save command is issued.
Apply saves provider configuration without activating a model.
Explicit Use activates the selected model and refreshes state.
Dirty-editor cancel can be declined or accepted.
Delete confirmation names the provider; cancel retains it and confirm clears the active provider/model.
Fetch loading disables provider/model fields and Save, then restores controls when complete.
An empty Fetch response shows an empty state.
A Fetch failure preserves the editor and can be retried successfully.
Fetch retains a stored key only when requested; clear-key intent omits both providerId and apiKey.
screenshots: Three temporary screenshots were produced under /private/tmp/noltri-ui-mock-qa/ (provider list, editor, fetch candidates); they are not committed.
limitations: This is built-UI browser automation with a mock Tauri bridge, not native-app/Tauri-command GUI validation.
Native System Events access to the candidate process returned macOS error -10827; no permission changes were made.
